newsitem.title: FRANCE: Seita falls on job cuts, Liggett deal.
newsitem.headline: Seita falls on job cuts, Liggett deal.

text.p: Shares in tobacco company Seita fell on Friday, on news of a U.S. legal settlement by the Liggett Group and the French company's decision to axe 300 jobs within 17 months, analysts said.
Seita stock was down 2.41 percent at 206.5 francs, on volume of 48,833 shares at 1230 GMT. The market was up 1.42 percent.

The Seita layoffs were seen as a sign of a faster- than-expected fall in smoking, analysts said. "The Seita announcement confirms the decline of dark tobacco consumption," said one analyst, who pointed out that Seita produces more dark than light tobacco and the former accounts for 50 percent of sales.
Seita said on Wednesday it would close its Chateauroux factory in western France, due to declining sales of dark tobacco cigarettes. The plant employs 280.
It planned to offer jobs to some 200 aged under 55 at another plant in Nantes, on the western coast and other measures were envisaged for those aged 55 and over.
Seita closed factories in Dijon and Macon, central France, in 1993.
One analyst said the Liggett legal settlement was unprecedented and weighed on the whole tobacco sector.

Under the terms of the deal, Liggett admits the health hazards of smoking and will pay 22 states a quarter of its pre-tax profits over the next 25 years, as well as a one-off $25 million payment. It will also allow current and former employees to testify against the rest of the industry.
